stops.name: Centennial Park
stops.notes: Small town park with picnic area

stops.name: Centerville City Park
stops.notes: Shady park near the largest courthouse square in the U.S. Easy, walkable leg-stretch.

stops.name: Judge Lewis Park
stops.notes: Park on the western edge of town with a paved walking loop and restrooms.

stops.name: Pioneer Park
stops.notes: Right on Highway 2 between Clarinda and Shenandoah. Picnic shelters, restrooms, fishing pond. A classic drive-break spot; also has RV camping with hookups and a dump station.

stops.name: Arbor Lodge State Historical Park
stops.notes: Birthplace of Arbor Day. Large shaded arboretum and picnic grounds. Mansion open Tue-Sun 11am-5pm (grounds open daily).

stops.name: Crete City Park
stops.notes: Right on NE-33. Good midpoint between Nebraska City and Hastings.

stops.name: North Park
stops.notes: Shade trees, picnic tables, and a nice lake. Holdrege also has another park just south of US-34 on Burlington St. and an inexpensive, level city campground for overnighting on East Ave just south of the tracks. Open 24 hours.

stops.name: Barnett Park
stops.notes: Attractive town park on several small lakes a few blocks south of US-34. Hours: 6:00 AM - 11:00 PM.

stops.name: Ward Bond Memorial Park
stops.notes: Green and shady with picnic tables and pavilions. May have city RV sites.

stops.name: Yuma City Park
stops.notes: Town park near the Colorado-Nebraska border, six blocks from US-34.

stops.name: Riverside Park
stops.notes: A genuine oasis on the plains. Riverside nature trails, disc golf, large shaded picnic areas. Hours: 5:00 AM - 11:00 PM.

stops.name: Viestenz-Smith Mountain Park
stops.notes: Right on US-34 in the canyon. Shaded riverside picnic tables and a CCC-built shelter. Last good pause before the winding climb to Estes Park. Check seasonal opening before relying on it. Hours: 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM.

stops.name: Howard T. Sawhill City Park
stops.notes: Town-square park with a band shell, oval amphitheater, and central fountain.

stops.name: Lake Atwood
stops.notes: Small city lake just north of US-36 with shaded picnic areas and fishing; a quick, walkable break in Atwood.

stops.name: Oberlin City Park
stops.notes: In-town city park right off US-36 — a shaded spot for a quick leg-stretch in the middle of Oberlin.

stops.name: Elmwood Park
stops.notes: Norton's shaded city park with picnic tables and restrooms; a good plains stretch-break.

stops.name: Phillipsburg City Park
stops.notes: Shaded in-town park with picnic tables — a straightforward break in the county seat.

stops.name: Wagner Park
stops.notes: County-seat park near the historic Old Dutch Mill; mature shade trees and picnic tables make a pleasant midpoint stop.

stops.name: Mankato City Park
stops.notes: Quiet county-seat city park for a quick leg-stretch.

stops.name: Belleville City Park
stops.notes: Shaded in-town city park, an easy break along US-36.

stops.name: Washington City Park
stops.notes: City Park with three covered picnic shelters.

stops.name: Marysville City Park
stops.notes: Home of Marysville's famous black squirrels. Big shaded park with restrooms an old train engine.

stops.name: Seneca City Park
stops.notes: Shaded city park with shelter houses and restrooms near the west side of town; South Park on the south side also has a picnic shelter and restrooms.

stops.name: Hiawatha City Lake Park
stops.notes: City lake park near the US-36/US-73 junction with picnic areas and fishing; an easy stretch-break.

stops.name: Krug Park
stops.notes: Large historic city park with a lagoon, gardens, and shaded picnic areas.

stops.name: Lyons Park
stops.notes: Small town park on the far outskirts of Denver.

stops.name: Memorial Park
stops.notes: Shaded roadside grove and rest stop at the southwest corner of the US-36/SH-71 junction, with restrooms and picnic facilities. A famous oasis of trees on the treeless plains (a noted migrant-bird stopover).

stops.name: Cope Memorial Park
stops.notes: Cope's small town memorial park — a quick leg-stretch midway across the eastern Colorado plains.

stops.name: Veterans Memorial Park
stops.notes: Roadside park and rest area in tiny Joes with shade and picnic space.

stops.name: Bittersweet Park
stops.notes: Greeley's shaded city park with a small lake, walking paths, and picnic areas.

stops.name: Akron City Park
stops.notes: Tiny town park three blocks from US-34.

stops.name: Rainbow Park
stops.notes: Tree-shaded town park with covered picnic shelters and an extensive paved multi-use trail along the North Fork of the Republican River, right off US-34.

stops.name: Trenton Park
stops.notes: Small town park for a quick leg-stretch; Swanson Reservoir is just west of town for a longer break but requires entry permit.

stops.name: Cambridge City Park
stops.notes: Shaded city park in Cambridge in the Republican River valley — a good stop midway between McCook and Holdrege.

stops.name: Arapahoe South Park
stops.notes: Arapahoe's South Park: shaded city park with picnic space and a small camping area, an easy break on the US-6/US-34 run.

stops.name: Chautauqua Park
stops.notes: Town park near the railroad station with picnic tables and shade trees.

stops.name: Heartwell Park
stops.notes: Large shaded city park with a lagoon and picnic areas.  Two small parking lots, one on Lakeside Drive, the other on Forest Blvd.

stops.name: Sutton City Park
stops.notes: Shaded city park in Sutton, right on US-6 — an easy first break east of Hastings.

stops.name: Dorchester City Park
stops.notes: Small-town park in Dorchester on US-6

stops.name: Taggart Park
stops.notes: Town park in Palmyra along NE-2 between Lincoln and Nebraska City.

stops.name: Williams Park
stops.notes: Syracuse's city park, a short hop off the NE-2 bypass (N-50 exit) — the main town stop between US-77 and Nebraska City.

stops.name: Sidney City Park
stops.notes: Sidney's city park, just off the IA-2/US-275 bypass

stops.name: Clarinda City Park
stops.notes: City park in Clarinda (Glenn Miller's hometown) on IA-2 between Shenandoah and Bedford.

stops.name: Bibbins Park
stops.notes: Town park in Bedford, the Taylor County seat, on IA-2.

stops.name: Noel Park
stops.notes: City park in Leon on IA-2 (US-69 junction) between Mount Ayr and Corydon.

stops.name: Corydon Lake Park
stops.notes: Beautiful, quiet, clean park on a lake at the western edge of Corydon right off of IA-2.

stops.name: Roddy Road Park
stops.notes: Frederick County park beside the 1856 Roddy Road covered bridge, just off US-15 north of Thurmont — picnic shelter, tables, grills, and Owens Creek access.

stops.name: Mason-Dixon Welcome Center
stops.notes: Maryland welcome center on southbound US-15 just south of the Pennsylvania line — restrooms, vending, pet area, picnic tables, RV parking, and a Catoctin Mountains overlook.

stops.name: Point of Rocks Community Commons Park
stops.notes: Small community park by the historic Point of Rocks train station on the Potomac — picnic shelter, restrooms, trails, amphitheater, and C&O Canal towpath access.

stops.name: South Mountain Eastbound Welcome Center
stops.notes: Maryland welcome center on I-70 eastbound atop South Mountain (mile 39) — restrooms, playground, travel info, and RV/truck/car parking.

stops.name: South Mountain Westbound Welcome Center
stops.notes: Maryland welcome center on I-70 westbound atop South Mountain (mile 39) — restrooms, playground, travel info, and RV/truck/car parking.

stops.name: Crystal Spring Rest Area (I-70)
stops.notes: Pennsylvania rest area on I-70 eastbound (signed East, but runs south toward Hancock/MD) — the first rest area south of Breezewood. Restrooms, vending, and picnic tables.

stops.name: Marty Snook Memorial Park
stops.notes: Washington County park south of Hagerstown — tennis courts, picnic areas, and a large parking lot right at the entrance. Easy in-and-out off I-70/I-81.

stops.name: Pennsylvania Welcome Center
stops.notes: PennDOT welcome center with restrooms, vending, and tourist information, just inside Pennsylvania.

stops.name: Highspire Service Plaza
stops.notes: PA Turnpike service plaza — restrooms, Roy Rogers, Starbucks, and Sunoco fuel. Open to all turnpike traffic; no exit needed.

stops.name: Lawn Service Plaza
stops.notes: PA Turnpike service plaza — restrooms, tourist information, Burger King, Starbucks, Hershey's ice cream, and outdoor seating. No exit needed.

stops.name: Lake Rowena Park
stops.notes: Ebensburg's lake park — restrooms, playground, picnic shelters, a fire pit, skate park, and a fenced community dog park. One of the better leg-stretch stops on US-22.

stops.name: Bomansville Service Plaza
stops.notes: PA Turnpike service plaza — restrooms, Sunoco fuel, and a Tesla Supercharger. No exit needed.

stops.name: Recreation Park
stops.notes: Cameron's city park — restrooms, playground, picnic areas, ballfields, and a pool, with free parking right off the road.

stops.name: Westview Park
stops.notes: Donnellson's city park on IA-2 just west of town — shelter houses with restrooms, ball fields, and a playground.

stops.name: Waubonsie Trail Park
stops.notes: Cantril's 23-acre city park on the northwest edge of town — picnic shelters, a pond ringed by a ~1-mile gravel trail with three covered bridges, disc golf, and a few campsites. Next to the Dutchman's Store, a Mennonite general store.

stops.name: Indian Lake Park
stops.notes: 177-acre city park on the lake just outside Farmington — open and enclosed picnic shelters, a stone lodge, a modern bathhouse, fishing, and trails.

stops.name: Riverview Park
stops.notes: Mississippi riverfront park in Fort Madison — open picnic shelter, restrooms, a riverwalk, gardens, a Santa Fe steam locomotive, and Old Fort Madison.

stops.name: Monmouth Park
stops.notes: Monmouth's main city park, just off US-34 on N. 11th Street — picnic shelters, a gazebo, band shell, playgrounds, and courts.

stops.name: Lake Storey Park
stops.notes: Lakeside recreation park on the north side of Galesburg near US-34 — picnic shelters, grills, a nature center, and lake views.

stops.name: McCorkle Park
stops.notes: Cameron's downtown city park at 100 W. Third Street — the Price Pavilion picnic shelter, picnic areas, and benches.

stops.name: J.C. Penney Park
stops.notes: Small downtown park in Hamilton at Davis (MO-13) and McGaughy, beside the J.C. Penney boyhood-home museum — picnic tables and shade; site of the Saturday-morning farmers market. Hamilton is "Quilt Town USA," home of the Missouri Star Quilt Co.

stops.name: Simpson Park
stops.notes: Chillicothe's ~36-acre city park on Washington Street (US-65) — picnic shelters with electricity, playgrounds, tennis, and old-growth shade trees. Chillicothe is the "Home of Sliced Bread."

stops.name: South City Park
stops.notes: Brookfield's 43-acre city park, entered from Image Road off MO-11 — picnic shelters, several playgrounds, a disc-golf course, and horseshoe pits.

stops.name: Macon Lake Park
stops.notes: City park on Macon Lake — restrooms, picnic shelter, and a boat ramp. Parking is right at the water.

stops.name: Shelbina Lake Park
stops.notes: WPA-built lake park about 2 miles north of Shelbina on MO-15 — five picnic shelters, restrooms, fishing and boating, a 9-hole grass-green golf course, and a playground.

stops.name: South Park
stops.notes: City park on the south side of Monroe City — covered picnic pavilion, playground, and open green space.

stops.name: Riverview Park
stops.notes: 465-acre bluff-top park on the north edge of Hannibal — two Mississippi River overlooks, the Mark Twain statue, picnic tables and pavilions, restrooms, and wooded trails.

stops.name: Bloomfield City Park
stops.notes: Bloomfield's city park, just off IA-2/US-63 — a picnic area with two pavilions, restrooms, a playground, and a covered bridge, plus courts, ball fields, and frisbee golf.

stops.name: Peterson Park
stops.notes: City park one block north of IL-16 on the northeast side of Mattoon — picnic tables and shelters, restrooms, playground, band shell, and an aquatic center. Quick to reach from the highway.

stops.name: Cooper Commons
stops.notes: Town park on the north bank of the White River at the south edge of Spencer, just off IN-46 — shelter houses, open fields, playgrounds, and restrooms. Convenient leg-stretch between Terre Haute and Bloomington.

stops.name: Lower Cascades Park
stops.notes: Wooded ravine park on the north side of Bloomington — picnic tables, shelters, a playground, and a paved trail with boardwalk, with seasonal restrooms.

stops.name: Mill Race Park
stops.notes: 85-acre riverfront park in downtown Columbus on an oxbow of the Flatrock River — picnic shelters, an 84-ft observation tower, a historic covered bridge, fishing lakes, playground, and seasonal restrooms.

stops.name: Tripton Park
stops.notes: North Vernon city park — paved trails, a boardwalk, an outdoor amphitheater, fishing, playground, and a welcome center with restrooms.

stops.name: Bicentennial Park
stops.notes: Riverfront park on Madison's Ohio River waterfront downtown — open lawn and event space with ADA-accessible restrooms, water, and WiFi, river views, and the walkable historic downtown alongside.

stops.name: Great Crossing Park
stops.notes: Scott County park on Elkhorn Creek — picnic shelter, boat ramp, and parking at the launch. Quiet, quick stop off US-460.

stops.name: Garrard Park
stops.notes: City of Paris park near downtown — picnic area, playground, sports courts, restrooms, and water. Central, easy in-town stop.

stops.name: Easy Walker Park
stops.notes: Mount Sterling's main Montgomery County park on Osborne Road — a picnic shelter with grills, playground, walking trail, ball fields, a fishing pond, and restrooms (portable when the building is locked).

stops.name: Morton Park
stops.notes: Charleston city park — playground, picnic shelter, and ballfields, with fast food (Taco Bell, Subway) right across the street.

stops.name: Clear Creek Welcome Center (I-70 EB)
stops.notes: INDOT welcome center on I-70 eastbound at MM 2, about 2 mi inside the Indiana line — rebuilt and reopened November 2025 with restrooms, walking path, dog park, and extra truck parking; Indy 500 theming inside. Eastbound only; the westbound counterpart is the Cumberland Road Welcome Center about 9 mi away in Illinois.

stops.name: I-64 East Rest Area
stops.notes: Kentucky rest area on I-64 eastbound near Morehead, opposite the westbound side.

stops.name: I-64 West Rest Area
stops.notes: Rest area on I-64 westbound near Morehead — picnic tables.

stops.name: Nichols Park
stops.notes: Jacksonville's largest city park — open-air pavilion, pool, and a roller hockey rink, with plenty of room to walk.

stops.name: Wyman Park
stops.notes: Sullivan city park with ballfields — a simple, quiet leg-stretch off IL-32.

stops.name: Fletcher Park
stops.notes: Mount Zion village park — playground, picnic shelter, community center, and parking right at the entrance.

stops.name: Tom Madonia Park
stops.notes: Springfield city park — picnic tables, playground, and dedicated parking; a quick stop off the west side of town.

stops.name: Barry Travel Plaza
stops.notes: Roady's truck stop at I-72 exit 20 in Barry — fuel, food, and truck parking. Barry is the only town on I-72 between the Mississippi and Jacksonville, so it's the practical mid-route stop.

stops.name: Ebaugh County Park
stops.notes: Small Scott County park just off I-72.

stops.name: I-64 East Rest Area
stops.notes: Kentucky rest area on I-64 eastbound near Grayson — restrooms.

stops.name: I-64 West Rest Area
stops.notes: Kentucky rest area on I-64 westbound near Grayson — restrooms, picnic tables and shelter, grills, vending, and benches. The better-equipped of the Grayson pair.

stops.name: I-64 East Rest Area
stops.notes: West Virginia rest area on I-64 eastbound near Huntington — restrooms, picnic tables, free parking.

stops.name: I-64 East Rest Area
stops.notes: West Virginia rest area on I-64 eastbound at Culloden — restrooms.

stops.name: I-64 West Rest Area
stops.notes: West Virginia rest area on I-64 westbound at Culloden — restrooms.

stops.name: I-79 North Rest Area
stops.notes: Frametown rest area on I-79 northbound — picnic tables and parking.

stops.name: I-79 South Rest Area
stops.notes: Frametown rest area on I-79 southbound — restrooms, picnic area, and a free RV sanitary dump station.

stops.name: I-79 North Rest Area
stops.notes: West Virginia rest area on I-79 northbound near Burnsville — restrooms.

stops.name: I-79 South Rest Area
stops.notes: West Virginia rest area on I-79 southbound near Burnsville — restrooms.

stops.name: Mount Storm Scenic Overlook
stops.notes: Paved scenic overlook pull-off on US-48 (Corridor H) in the Allegheny Front high country near Mount Storm.

stops.name: Corridor H Scenic Overlook
stops.notes: Paved scenic overlook with parking loop on US-48 (Corridor H) in the Hardy County mountains.

stops.name: Clifford Hollow Bridge Overlook
stops.notes: Paved overlook parking beside US-48 (Corridor H) at the Clifford Hollow Bridge, one of the highway's tall valley spans.

stops.name: Casselman River Bridge State Park
stops.notes: Small day-use state park on US-40 (the National Road) preserving the 1813 Casselman River stone arch bridge; riverside picnic area and parking.

stops.name: Fort Necessity National Battlefield
stops.notes: National Park Service battlefield on US-40 (the National Road) with a visitor center, picnic area, restrooms, and the historic Mount Washington Tavern.

stops.name: National Road Watering Trough
stops.notes: Historic stone watering trough pull-off on US-40 (the National Road) atop Chestnut Ridge.

stops.name: I-70 East Rest Area
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area and Pennsylvania Welcome Center on I-70 eastbound at West Alexander, just inside the state line — restrooms, tourist information, free parking.

stops.name: I-70 West Rest Area
stops.notes: ODOT Belmont rest area on I-70 westbound — restrooms, drinking water, vending, picnic tables and shelter, free parking.

stops.name: I-70 East Rest Area
stops.notes: ODOT Belmont rest area on I-70 eastbound — restrooms, drinking water, vending, picnic tables, free parking.

stops.name: I-70 West Rest Area
stops.notes: ODOT rest area on I-70 westbound near Norwich — restrooms and free parking.

stops.name: Sideling Hill Rest Area (Eastbound)
stops.notes: I-68 rest area at the Sideling Hill road cut (exposed syncline), ~6 mi west of Hancock; a pedestrian footbridge over the interstate links the two sides and the former exhibit center.

stops.name: Sideling Hill Rest Area (Westbound)
stops.notes: I-68 rest area at the Sideling Hill road cut (exposed syncline), ~6 mi west of Hancock; a pedestrian footbridge over the interstate links the two sides and the former exhibit center.

stops.name: Dillion State Park
stops.notes: Day-use area at Dillon State Park — tennis and basketball courts, beach volleyball, and parking at the entrance. Just off I-70 west of Zanesville.

stops.name: Everett Park
stops.notes: Small Newark city park — a quiet residential-neighborhood stop.

stops.name: Sharon Woods Metro Park
stops.notes: Columbus-area metro park — picnic tables, shelter, grills, and free parking; room for a real walk rather than just a stretch.

stops.name: Indian Lake State Park
stops.notes: Day-use area on Indian Lake with boat ramps and parking — a quick water stop off US-33.

stops.name: Jaycee Park
stops.notes: Wapakoneta city park — playground, basketball court, and parking; a short hop off I-75.

stops.name: Rutan Park
stops.notes: Town park with a playground, tennis and pickleball courts, and parking right at the entrance.

stops.name: American Legion Park
stops.notes: Marysville park complex — restrooms, playground, pool, and the adjacent Memorial Park.

stops.name: Borough of Cokeburg Park
stops.notes: Cokeburg borough park — ballfield, batting cage, and playground, next to the borough building and post office.

stops.name: Centerview Park
stops.notes: Village park with tennis courts and open ground — a simple leg-stretch stop.

stops.name: Lehman Park
stops.notes: Berne town park — ballfields and open ground, with parking on the near side.

stops.name: Tower Park
stops.notes: Town park with ballfields — a quick, quiet stop.

stops.name: Maconaquah Park
stops.notes: Peru city park on the Wabash — restrooms, playground, basketball, an amphitheater, and several numbered picnic shelters. One of the better stops on US-24/US-31.

stops.name: Fairview Park
stops.notes: Logansport city park — restrooms, basketball court, and several ballfields.

stops.name: Altherr Nature Park
stops.notes: Small nature park with drinking water and benches, next to a CountryMark station and a theater — a short, quiet stretch stop.

stops.name: Rodger G. Wolcott Memorial Park
stops.notes: Wolcott town park — restrooms, picnic shelter, ballfield, and a community center, with parking at the entrance. Handy off US-24/I-65.

stops.name: Foster Park
stops.notes: Goodland town park — playground, picnic shelter, and a basketball court.

stops.name: Kay Park
stops.notes: Watseka city park — ballfields and open ground, adjoining Forest Park; a McDonald's is a block away.

stops.name: Mann Park
stops.notes: Gilman village park with a ballfield — a simple stop off I-57/US-24.

stops.name: Main City Park
stops.notes: Chenoa's main park, run by the Chenoa Park District — ballfield and open ground in the middle of town, near the city hall and post office. Quick hop off I-55.

stops.name: Eureka Lake Park
stops.notes: Eureka's lake park — picnic shelter with tables, grills, a playground, a picnic site by the water, and the Eureka Lake Pavilion. A pleasant stop off I-74.

stops.name: Mackinaw Dells Rest Area Westbound
stops.notes: IDOT rest area on I-74 westbound at the Mackinaw River — restrooms, parking, and a playground.

stops.name: Mackinaw Dells Rest Area Eastbound
stops.notes: IDOT rest area on I-74 eastbound at the Mackinaw River, opposite the westbound side.

stops.name: Spoon River Rest Area Westbound
stops.notes: IDOT rest area on I-74 westbound at the Spoon River — parking and restrooms.

stops.name: Spoon River Rest Area Eastbound
stops.notes: IDOT rest area on I-74 eastbound at the Spoon River — picnic tables and a covered picnic shelter, free parking.

stops.name: Lakewood Park
stops.notes: Morton Park District's lake park — picnic site with tables, vending, a boat ramp, and free parking right at the water. Dogs allowed on leash. Easy stop off I-74.

stops.name: Chatsworth Community Park
stops.notes: Chatsworth's community park — open ground for a quiet leg-stretch.

stops.name: Earl New Veteran's Memorial
stops.notes: Small roadside veterans' memorial in the village of Gratz — a monument stop rather than a park.

stops.name: Claysburg Community Park
stops.notes: Claysburg community park — playground, ballfield, restrooms, and parking at the entrance. Convenient off I-99/US-220.

stops.name: Snake Spring Community Park
stops.notes: Community park with a picnic shelter, playground, and ballfield — a quiet stop near the Bedford I-70/I-99 interchange.

stops.name: Yellow Creek Lake
stops.notes: Boat launch and day-use area on the 720-acre lake at Yellow Creek State Park, between Indiana and Blairsville on US-422.

stops.name: Kittanning Riverfront Park
stops.notes: Kittanning's park on the Allegheny River — restrooms, boat ramp, and riverfront parking, with a Sheetz and Dunkin' a block up.

stops.name: Ritts Park
stops.notes: Town park with a picnic shelter, playground, basketball court, and open grass.

stops.name: Fort Hunter Mansion and Park
stops.notes: Dauphin County's historic riverside estate on the Susquehanna — mansion and grounds with picnic tables, restrooms, and parking. More interesting than a plain rest stop if you have a few extra minutes.

stops.name: Millerstown Area Community Park
stops.notes: Millerstown's community park — playground and open ground along the Juniata, just off US-322/US-22.

stops.name: Lewistown Viscose WWII Memorial
stops.notes: Small memorial site with its own parking, on the edge of Lewistown. No facilities — a monument stop rather than a park.

stops.name: Oak Hall Regional Park
stops.notes: Centre Region regional park near State College — restrooms, drinking water, ballfields, and parking. Room for a real walk.

stops.name: Slabtown Park
stops.notes: Philipsburg town park — restrooms, basketball court, and bleachers.

stops.name: Jefferson County Rest Area Westbound
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-80 westbound in Jefferson County — restrooms, picnic tables, and separate car and truck parking, all free.

stops.name: Jefferson County Rest Area Eastbound
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-80 eastbound in Jefferson County — restrooms with separate car and truck parking, free.

stops.name: Kurtz Nature Park
stops.notes: Clearfield nature park — picnic shelter, basketball court, and parking at the entrance.

stops.name: Burgess Park
stops.notes: Titusville city park — playground, tennis courts, and a swimming facility, with parking at the entrance.

stops.name: Blandon Fire Company Park
stops.notes: Fire-company park in Blandon — playground and basketball court, run by Blandon Fire Company No. 1.

stops.name: Port Clinton Park
stops.notes: Small borough park at Port Clinton on the Schuylkill — basketball court, a primitive kayak launch, and the Appalachian Trail / Schuylkill River trailhead parking next door.

stops.name: Montour County Rest Area Westbound
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-80 westbound in Montour County — restrooms and free parking.

stops.name: Montour County Rest Area Eastbound
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-80 eastbound in Montour County — restrooms, picnic tables and shelter, separate car and truck parking, free.

stops.name: Clinton County Rest Area Eastbound
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-80 eastbound in Clinton County — restrooms with separate car and truck parking.

stops.name: Clinton County Rest Area Westbound
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-80 westbound in Clinton County — restrooms with separate car and truck parking, free.

stops.name: Centre County Rest Area Westbound
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-80 westbound at Snow Shoe — restrooms with separate car and truck parking, free.

stops.name: Centre County Rest Area Eastbound
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-80 eastbound at Snow Shoe — restrooms and picnic tables, free parking.

stops.name: River View Park
stops.notes: Riverside town park — restrooms, picnic shelter, playground, and parking right at the entrance.

stops.name: Renovo 16th Street Park
stops.notes: Renovo Borough's park — restrooms, picnic shelter, and borough-run parking, with an information board on site.

stops.name: Mount Carmel Township Municipal Building
stops.notes: Township municipal building with a basketball court and small park alongside; the police and fire companies share the lot. A parking-lot stretch stop, not a destination.

stops.name: Blue Mountain Service Plaza
stops.notes: PA Turnpike service plaza — restrooms, Roy Rogers, Sbarro, Auntie Anne's, Starbucks, and free parking. No exit needed.

stops.name: Sideling Hill Service Plaza
stops.notes: PA Turnpike service plaza — restrooms, Burger King, Popeyes, Auntie Anne's, Famiglia Pizzeria, Starbucks, and outdoor seating. No exit needed.

stops.name: Cumberland Valley Service Plaza
stops.notes: PA Turnpike service plaza — restrooms, Roy Rogers, Starbucks, and free parking. No exit needed.

stops.name: Tyrone History Museum
stops.notes: Tyrone Historical Society's museum with its own parking and a small park alongside — a short, interesting break off US-220.

stops.name: Venango County Rest Area Eastbound
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-80 eastbound in Venango County — restrooms with separate car and truck parking, free.

stops.name: Venango County Rest Area Westbound
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-80 westbound in Venango County — restrooms with separate car and truck parking, free.

stops.name: Riverside Park
stops.notes: Greenville's park on the Shenango — playground, basketball court, and parking.

stops.name: Peter J. Camiel Service Plaza
stops.notes: PA Turnpike service plaza near Elverson — Roy Rogers, Dunkin', Starbucks, Sunoco fuel, and a Tesla Supercharger.

stops.name: Woodburn Park
stops.notes: Shippenville village park — picnic shelter, playground, and a volleyball court, with parking at the entrance.

stops.name: Gazebo Park
stops.notes: Waterford borough's small green in the center of town — gazebo, shelter, and a ballfield, with a pharmacy and several restaurants right around it.

stops.name: Riverfront Park
stops.notes: Franklin's park along the Allegheny — benches, tennis courts, and open riverfront walking.

stops.name: Bicentennial Park
stops.notes: Meadville city park on French Creek — restrooms, picnic shelter, playground, boat ramp, and free parking.

stops.name: I-79 North Rest Area
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-79 northbound in Crawford County — restrooms and parking.

stops.name: I-79 South Rest Area
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-79 southbound in Crawford County — restrooms and parking.

stops.name: I-79 South Rest Area
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-79 southbound in Lawrence County — restrooms, vending, and a picnic site.

stops.name: I-79 North Rest Area
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-79 northbound in Lawrence County — restrooms, vending, picnic tables, and free parking.

stops.name: I-79 North Rest Area
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-79 northbound in Crawford County, near the Ohio line.

stops.name: I-79 South Rest Area
stops.notes: PennDOT rest area on I-79 southbound in Crawford County — restrooms.

stops.name: Picnic Area
stops.notes: Roadside picnic site on US-50 at Mardela Springs — tables only, no other facilities.

stops.name: Ferry Point Park
stops.notes: Queen Anne's County park at Kent Narrows — boat ramp, nature reserve, and the Chesapeake Heritage Center, with parking right off US-50. A good Eastern Shore break.

stops.name: Letterkenny Reservoir
stops.notes: 58-acre water-supply reservoir with a public boat launch and fishing access under a PA Fish & Boat Commission agreement. A quiet water stop; no developed facilities confirmed.

stops.name: Riverside Park
stops.notes: Huntingdon's park on the Juniata — picnic shelter, playground, horseshoe pits, benches, and parking at the entrance.

stops.name: Pilot Flying J Travel Center #686
stops.notes: 24-hr Pilot/Flying J travel center at I-80 Exit 432 (Hwy 31), 15010 NE-31, on the hill locally called Melia Hill. ~150 truck/RV overnight spaces, 2 RV fuel lanes, RV dump station ($10 / $7.50 w/ card), showers, CAT scale, Denny's.

stops.name: Melia Hill Rest Area (I-80 WB)
stops.notes: NDOT westbound I-80 safety rest area (MM 431.6), ~2 mi west of the Hwy 31 interchange; restrooms, truck & car parking, picnic shelters, seasonal welcome center. No RV dump station.

stops.name: Platte River Rest Area (I-80 EB)
stops.notes: NDOT eastbound I-80 safety rest area (MM 425.1), ~4 mi east of Greenwood; restrooms, water, pull-through parking (~10 trucks/44 cars), picnic shelters. Has an RV dump station.

stops.name: Blue River Rest Area (I-80 EB)
stops.notes: NDOT eastbound I-80 safety rest area (MM 381.5), ~1 mi west of the Milford interchange; restrooms, water, truck & car parking, picnic shelters. Has an RV dump station.

stops.name: Goehner Rest Area (I-80 WB)
stops.notes: NDOT westbound I-80 rest area (MM 375), ~2 mi east of the Goehner interchange; restrooms and parking. No RV dump station.

stops.name: York Rest Area / Welcome Center (I-80 WB)
stops.notes: NDOT westbound I-80 safety rest area / welcome-visitor center (MM 355.2), ~3 mi east of the York interchange; restrooms, water, truck & car parking. Has an RV dump station.

stops.name: York Rest Area (I-80 EB)
stops.notes: NDOT eastbound I-80 safety rest area / welcome-visitor center (MM 350.8), ~3 mi west of the York interchange; restrooms, water, truck & car parking. No RV dump station (the dump is at the York westbound rest area).

stops.name: Grand Island Rest Area (I-80 WB)
stops.notes: NDOT westbound I-80 safety rest area (MM 316.5), ~3 mi west of the Phillips/US-281 interchange; restrooms, truck & car parking. No RV dump station.

stops.name: Grand Island Rest Area (I-80 EB)
stops.notes: NDOT eastbound I-80 safety rest area (MM 314.9), ~4 mi west of the Phillips/US-281 interchange; restrooms, truck & car parking. No RV dump station.

stops.name: Kearney Rest Area / Welcome Center (I-80 WB)
stops.notes: NDOT westbound I-80 welcome-visitor center (MM 270.9), ~2 mi west of Kearney (22-acre site with a small fishing lake); restrooms, truck & car parking, picnic shelters, playground. No RV dump station. The Great Platte River Road Archway monument spans I-80 near Exit 275, just east.

stops.name: Kearney Rest Area / Welcome Center (I-80 EB)
stops.notes: NDOT eastbound I-80 welcome-visitor center (MM 269.0), ~3 mi west of Kearney; restrooms, truck & car parking, picnic shelters. No RV dump station. Westernmost I-80 rest area east of Elm Creek (MM 257).

stops.name: Mill Race Park
stops.notes: Parsons city park (~16.6 acres) along the Black Fork of the Cheat River just off US-219 — day-use park with four picnic pavilions, a splash-park zone, tennis court, playgrounds, outdoor exercise stations, a walking trail, and public restrooms. A pleasant riverside leg-stretch stop (no camping at this park; the RV-camping blurb that circulates online actually belongs to a same-named park in Atkinson, NE).

stops.name: North End Park
stops.notes: Buckhannon city park on Cleveland Avenue at the north end of town, on the Buckhannon River (also signed North Buckhannon Riverfront Park) — soccer field, playground, restrooms, picnic pavilions, river access, and a perimeter walking/biking path. A quiet in-town leg-stretch stop; city parks are open sunrise to sunset.

stops.name: Eagle Community Park
stops.notes: Village park just north of US-34 (O St) on the west side of Eagle — ball diamond, tennis and sand-volleyball courts, playground, and picnic tables. A quick leg-stretch on the run east of Lincoln.

stops.name: Memorial Park
stops.notes: Plattsmouth's main park complex in the southwest part of town — three covered picnic shelters, ball fields, restrooms, and lighted tennis/basketball courts. About a mile east of the US-34/US-75 corridor; the last town before US-34 crosses the Missouri River into Iowa.

stops.name: Glenwood Lake Park
stops.notes: Right at the US-34/US-275 junction on the east edge of Glenwood — a 15-acre lake ringed by picnic shelters with grills, a playground, and a walking trail. First good stop east of the Missouri River.

stops.name: Chautauqua Park
stops.notes: Red Oak's park under the city water tower — a large picnic pavilion, shaded tables, ball field, sledding hill, and play areas. About a mile south of US-34 through town.

stops.name: Spring Lake Park
stops.notes: Adams County park right at the US-34/IA-148 junction on the south edge of Corning — a picnic area beside a spring-fed lake and restored wetland, with ball fields. For a shadier sit-down, downtown Central Park (8th St, ~half a mile north) has a newer pavilion and a veterans memorial.

stops.name: McKinley Park
stops.notes: Creston's big park just north of US-34 — an 11-acre pond, eight picnic shelters of various sizes, a band shell, playgrounds, and a swimming pool. Trailhead for the paved path out to Green Valley State Park.

stops.name: East Lake Park
stops.notes: Clarke County's oak-shaded lake park right on US-34 just east of Osceola — picnic shelters, playgrounds, an overlook tower, sand volleyball, and hiking/paved trails around a 15-acre lake. Easy in-and-out off the highway.

stops.name: Red Haw State Park
stops.notes: Free day-use state park on Red Haw Lake, its entrance right on US-34 just east of Chariton — lakeside picnic shelters and tables under the trees, famous for its redbud bloom in spring. An easy, scenic pause.

stops.name: Albia City Park
stops.notes: Albia's central park near the US-34/IA-5/IA-137 junction — picnic shelter, ball fields, tennis courts, a walking track, a small pond, and a playground. A block off the Victorian town square.

stops.name: Greater Ottumwa Park
stops.notes: A sprawling 340-acre park along the Des Moines River immediately south of US-34 — picnic shelters with grills, playgrounds, ball fields, ponds, and miles of trail. Plenty of room to stretch and picnic right off the highway.

stops.name: Chautauqua Park
stops.notes: Fairfield's 28.7-acre Chautauqua Park on E Burlington Ave (the Business US-34 route through town, a short hop north off the bypass) — four shelter houses, picnic and playground areas, restrooms, and a disc-golf course.

stops.name: McMillan Park
stops.notes: The Old Threshers Reunion grounds on the south side of Mount Pleasant, about half a mile south of US-34 — a picnic shelter house, restrooms, playground, and wide-open grounds with easy parking.

stops.name: Dan Daniel Memorial Park
stops.notes: Danville riverside park right off US-29 (the Danville Expressway) on the Dan River — picnic shelters, a playground, ball fields, a skate park, and an access point to the Danville Riverwalk Trail. Adjacent Anglers Park adds a boat ramp and more picnic tables.

stops.name: Larry M. Carroll Memorial Park
stops.notes: Baldwin's town park near the US-90/US-301 junction — two covered picnic areas with tables, a playground, and the 'Baldwin Station' brick trailhead pavilion (with a restored rail car) for the Jacksonville-Baldwin Rail Trail.

stops.name: Lochloosa Park
stops.notes: Small Alachua County park right on US-301 on the shore of Lochloosa Lake — a shaded picnic area, a gazebo, and a boardwalk over the marsh for wildlife viewing (alligators are common), plus a boat ramp. A quick, scenic leg-stretch.

stops.name: Lake Hernando Park
stops.notes: Citrus County lakefront park just east of US-41 in Hernando — two pavilions plus several picnic shelters, a playground, fishing docks, boardwalks, and shaded paths along Lake Hernando. ADA-friendly.

stops.name: Ewing Park
stops.notes: Nassau County's oak-shaded Ewing Memorial Park just east of the US-1/US-301 junction in Callahan — a pavilion and picnic tables under big oaks, a quarter-mile walking trail, a playground, tennis/basketball courts, and restrooms.

stops.name: Kiwanis Family Park
stops.notes: Sanford city/county park off Wicker St just east of US-1 — two picnic shelters, a splash pad, a playground, a half-mile paved walking loop, a gazebo, and picnic tables. Open dawn to dusk.

stops.name: Pleasant Grove Park
stops.notes: Fluvanna County's 900-acre Pleasant Grove Park right off US-15 in Palmyra — four picnic shelters and pavilions, ball fields, a dog park, and 20+ miles of trails including an ADA path to the Rivanna River. Farmers market on site.

stops.name: South Seagrove Welcome Center
stops.notes: NCDOT visitor center on US-220 (future I-73/I-74) about a mile south of Exit 61/NC-705 at Seagrove — 24-hour restrooms, covered picnic spots, car/RV/truck parking, and vending, plus a staffed welcome desk with 60+ Seagrove-pottery displays and statewide travel info. Southbound side of the twin I-73/74 centers.

stops.name: I-20 Eastbound Rest Area
stops.notes: SCDOT rest area on I-20 eastbound at Mile Marker 93.5 near Lugoff (Kershaw County) — restrooms, water, covered picnic tables, a pet-walk area, vending, and separate car/truck parking.

stops.name: English Park
stops.notes: Altavista's riverside town park on the Staunton River, right off US-29 about 20 miles south of Lynchburg — picnic shelters, a playground, ball fields, volleyball, walking trails, restrooms, and a canoe/boat launch. A good midpoint break on the US-29 run between Lynchburg and Danville.

stops.name: Cheraw State Park
stops.notes: The oldest state park in South Carolina, right off US-1 a few miles south of Cheraw — two picnic shelters (free first-come when unreserved) plus picnic pads, grills, and a playground along 360-acre Lake Juniper, with a swimming beach, a cypress-lake boardwalk, and boat rentals.

stops.name: Cracker Williams Park
stops.notes: Jesup community park (with a community center, pool, and courts) a short hop west of US-301 — a covered pavilion with restrooms and picnic tables, first-come when not reserved. A midway break on the US-301 run through southeast Georgia.

stops.name: Pioneer Park
stops.notes: A 115-acre Hardee County park right at the US-17/SR-64 junction in Zolfo Springs, on the Peace River — picnic pavilions, a big shaded grassy area, a playground, a boat ramp, trails, and a pioneer museum. Open 7 to 6.

stops.name: Spring Park
stops.notes: Green Cove Springs' riverfront park a block east of US-17 on the St. Johns River — picnic pavilions and tables under the oaks, a gazebo, a spring-fed swimming pool, a riverwalk, a fishing pier, and a playground.

stops.name: Wilck's Lake Park
stops.notes: Farmville's 150-acre natural area on the northwest edge of town right off US-15 — a 55-acre lake, picnic shelters and covered tables, a playground, a skate park, restrooms, and a 2-mile wooded trail around the lake.

stops.name: I-20 Westbound Rest Area
stops.notes: SCDOT rest area on I-20 westbound at Mile Marker 93.5 near Lugoff (Kershaw County), across from the eastbound rest area — restrooms, water, covered picnic tables, a pet-walk area, vending, and separate car/truck parking. Open 24 hours.

stops.name: North Seagrove Welcome Center
stops.notes: NCDOT visitor center on US-220 (future I-73/I-74) about a mile south of Exit 61/NC-705 at Seagrove — the northbound twin across the highway from the southbound center. Opened 2010: 24-hour restrooms, picnic tables and grills, a walking trail, landscaped grounds with a fountain, vending, and a staffed welcome desk with Seagrove-pottery displays.

stops.name: Port of Burlington Welcome Center
stops.notes: Official State of Iowa Welcome Center housed in the former Burlington Municipal Docks building, dedicated in 1928, with statewide info and souvenirs.  Open Wed-Sun 10-4

stops.name: Georgia Welcome Center
stops.notes: Georgia's US-301 welcome center near the South Carolina line — built in 1961, it is the oldest operating state welcome center in the country. Travel brochures and Georgia Grown products; open Tuesday-Saturday, 8:30-5:30, so check the day before counting on the building.

stops.name: Jackson-Baldwin Rail Trail parking lot
stops.notes:
Just a parking lot for the Jackson-Baldwin rail trail, but it's in a quiet wooded spot and is reasonable for a stretch break.  No facilities.

Also useful as a waypoint for a less-traveled routing between Ewing Memorial Park in Callahan and Spring Park in Green Cove Springs.

stops.name: Caravelle Ranch WMA
stops.notes: A well-maintained clearing with trees and a parking lot.  Decent spot for a stretch break.  No facilities.

stops.name: Patterson Park
stops.notes: Small park with a parking lot — a quiet pull-off stretch stop, no confirmed facilities.

stops.name: Lake Idamere Park
stops.notes: Lake County park north of Tavares — picnic shelters, playground, a Miracle League accessible ballfield, and bike parking.

stops.name: Polk State College - Lakeland
stops.notes: Community-college campus with visitor parking and a student center dining area — a workable stretch-and-coffee stop off I-4, not a park.

stops.name: Sunset Park
stops.notes: Babcock Ranch village park — restrooms and parking.

stops.name: Laishley Park
stops.notes: Punta Gorda's harborfront park — restrooms, drinking water, playground, fountain, picnic shelter, and the city marina. One of the nicer stops on this stretch.

stops.name: Freedom Park
stops.notes: Polk City's park — restrooms, drinking water, playground, and a picnic shelter, with parking on site.

stops.name: Lake David Park
stops.notes: Small waterfront town park with pavilion, pathways, and picnic tables.  Street parking only.

stops.name: Salt Springs Recreation Area
stops.notes: Facility may charge a day use fee which should be covered by a National Parks pass.

stops.name: Lake Dorr Recreation Area
stops.notes: Facility may charge a day use fee which should be covered by a National Parks pass.

stops.name: Storybook Park
stops.notes: Arcadia town park — playground and tennis courts.

stops.name: I-85 South Rest Area - Granville County
stops.notes: NCDOT rest area on I-85 southbound in Granville County — restrooms, drinking water, picnic tables, vending, and free parking.

stops.name: I-85 North Rest Area - Granville County
stops.notes: NCDOT rest area on I-85 northbound in Granville County — restrooms, drinking water, and free parking.

stops.name: Foxhaven Trail Parking
stops.notes: Just a parking lot for a trail, but a reasonable place for a stretch break.  No facilities.

stops.name: Fairview Heights Recreation Center
stops.notes: Lynchburg city recreation center — tennis courts, picnic tables, a small garden, and parking at the door.

stops.name: Fleetwood Hill Confederate Cavalry HQ
stops.notes: Fleetwood Hill at the Brandy Station battlefield, now part of Culpeper Battlefields State Park — paved parking and a 0.26-mile interpretive trail with ten signs and a viewfinder over the cavalry ground. About 30 minutes if you walk it; no facilities.

stops.name: W. D. James Park
stops.notes: Hamlet town park — playground, benches, and parking right at the entrance.

stops.name: Staunton View Park
stops.notes: Public use area on the John H. Kerr Reservoir backwater — open parkland, a quiet stop off US-58.

stops.name: Craig Park
stops.notes: Small park in downtown Chesterfield, beside the county library and courthouse.

stops.name: Town of Gaston Park
stops.notes: Gaston town park — running track and tennis courts next to Frances Mack Elementary, with parking on site.

stops.name: Edisto Memorial Gardens
stops.notes: Orangeburg's riverside gardens on the Edisto — restrooms, picnic shelter, fountain, and themed gardens (Serenity, Sensory) with parking at the entrance. Well worth the detour off I-26 if you have half an hour.

stops.name: George Roebuck Park
stops.notes: Small town park with playground, picnic pavilion, and ballfield.  May be useful as a routing waypoint to avoid Statesboro.

stops.name: Daisy Georgia Caboose
stops.notes: Just an old caboose in a tiny village.  No facilities.  Street parking only.  May be useful as a routing waypoint to avoid Fort Stewart and/or Statesboro.

stops.name: Cumberland Road Welcome Center (I-70 WB)
stops.notes: IDOT welcome center on I-70 westbound at MM 149, about 7 mi west of the Indiana line — restrooms, vending, picnic area, tourist information, separate truck and car parking. Sits on a rise with a view. Westbound only; the eastbound counterpart is the Clear Creek Welcome Center just inside Indiana.

stops.name: Westfield Village Park
stops.notes: Village park in the middle of Westfield, next to the town hall and post office, with a cafe and pub on the square.

stops.name: Massacre Canyon Rest Area
stops.notes: Historical monument and visitor center
